task_description: The script calculates geometric properties (area, perimeter) of a given polygon geometry after reprojection to EPSG:3857, and raster-based statistics (elevation mean/min/max and slope mean) from a DSM layer within that polygon. Elevation statistics are computed using QgsZonalStatistics directly on the input DSM layer; slope statistics require QGIS Processing framework initialization and execution of the 'native:slope' algorithm, followed by zonal statistics on the derived slope layer. If processing is unavailable, slope calculation is skipped and slope_mean remains None.

The script visualizes 3D solar energy and photovoltaic (PV) yield models using DSM (digital surface model), roof/ground irradiance or PV yield rasters, wall energy text files, and vegetation data. It loads geospatial layers into QGIS, allows interactive area selection via bounding rectangle, clips raster data to the selected extent using GDAL, reads clipped DSM and energy arrays into NumPy, processes wall energy data via a threaded worker, and renders a 3D OpenGL visualization with interactive controls (rotation, zoom, shift) and a dynamic colorbar scaled to irradiance [kWh/m²] or PV yield [kWh/kWp]. Outputs include an interactive 3D scene, colorbar legend, and optional screenshot export.
task_name: Visualize solar energy and photovoltaic yield

task_description: The script performs regression-based unmixing to estimate sub-pixel class fractions (e.g., endmember abundances) from a raster layer using synthetically mixed training data derived from a classification dataset of spectral endmembers. It constructs an ensemble of regressors (one per run), each trained on a unique synthetic mixture set generated via PrepareRegressionDatasetFromSynthMixAlgorithm; predicts fraction maps per class per run; aggregates predictions across runs using either mean±std or median±IQR (configurable); enforces optional sum-to-one constraint via raster math; outputs three rasters: (1) class fraction layer (multi-band, one band per class), (2) optional classification layer derived from argmax of fractions, and (3) optional variation layer (std or IQR per class). No specific study area, time range, satellite, or sensor is referenced — inputs are generic raster layers and classification datasets (e.g., .pkl endmember libraries), with no embedded temporal or platform metadata. All geospatial operations (stacking, aggregation, normalization, translation) are applied post-prediction using GDAL and EnMAP-Box algorithms.

The script performs a pixel-wise summation of multiple input binary (0/1) raster layers to produce a single output raster where each pixel value equals the count of input rasters with value 1 at that location. It uses QGIS’s QgsRasterCalculator to evaluate the formula 'raster1@1 + raster2@1 + ...' over the common extent and resolution of the first input raster. No normalization, classification, or external geospatial data (e.g., satellite imagery, time series, or study area definitions) is present in the code — it is a generic, geometry-agnostic raster algebra operation. Input rasters must be pre-binarized; no band selection, sensor processing, temporal filtering, or spatial subsetting occurs. The output is a GeoTIFF raster file named 'Boolean Overlay Map'.

The script performs a spatial constraint checking task by interrogating user-defined spatial datasets (e.g., PostGIS, Spatialite, SQL Server) for features intersecting or within a buffer of a query geometry (point, line, or polygon). It reads configuration from config.cfg and XG_SYS.ini, applies WHERE clauses to filter layers, computes distances, optionally includes descriptive fields, dates, and summary statistics, writes results to memory layers (point/line/polygon), inserts records into a configured database table (or creates a temporary one), and exports text/CSV reports. Outputs include a QGIS memory vector layer per geometry type, a tabular result model, and formatted text/CSV reports.

The script generates hypsometric curves from a digital elevation model (DEM) named 'dem_terrain.tif'. It first loads the DEM in QGIS, extracts its spatial extent and CRS, creates a boundary polygon matching that extent as a shapefile ('boundary.shp'), then runs the QGIS 'hypsometriccurves' algorithm with a 100-meter elevation step and percentage-based histogram output. The result is saved in the working directory as histogram files prefixed with 'histogram_' — indicating elevation distribution analysis by area percentage.

The script processes NLCD (National Land Cover Database) raster data for Alaska, specifically the 2016 Tree Canopy and Land Cover layers. It performs a sequence of geospatial operations: (1) reprojecting the input NLCD Land Cover raster to EPSG:4326; (2) reclassifying land cover classes into simplified grass-dominated values using a pixel-wise arithmetic expression mapping 20 original NLCD classes (e.g., 21=Developed, Open Space → 26; 41=Deciduous Forest → 23) to new integer codes; (3) separately reclassifying urban classes (21,22,23,24) into urban-subtype codes (10,1,1,2); (4) applying GRASS r.neighbors (median filter, size=7) to denoise and remove road/clutter artifacts from the urban layer; (5) compositing the cleaned urban layer over the grass-only layer using conditional pixel replacement (urban pixels override grass where present); (6) upscaling (8× finer resolution) via GDAL Warp with resampling; (7) spatially smoothing the high-resolution composite using GRASS r.neighbors (median, size=11); and (8) compressing and exporting as an 8-bit LZW-compressed GeoTIFF. The final output is a smoothed, high-resolution, urban-prioritized, grass-background land cover raster in WGS84, named 'NLCD_2016_Alaska_SaintPaul-Island_Smoothed-HD-Compressed_4326.tiff'. Input filenames and paths confirm the source is NLCD 2016, and the processing is explicitly scoped to Alaska, specifically Saint Paul Island and adjacent longitude bands (e.g., 'Alaska141-140_60').
task_name: Reclassify and smooth NLCD land cover

task_description: The script imports an EnMAP Level 1C product by reading its XML metadata file, extracting wavelength, FWHM, gain, and offset values per band, and generating a GDAL VRT raster file. It opens the corresponding SPECTRAL_IMAGE file (derived from the XML filename), sets ENVI metadata for wavelength (in nanometers) and FWHM, assigns band descriptions with center wavelengths, applies per-band scale (gain) and offset corrections via GDAL Band.SetScale/SetOffset, and flushes caches. The output is a calibrated, spectrally annotated VRT raster layer ready for analysis in EnMAP-Box; no classification, modeling, or time-series analysis is performed — only data import and radiometric scaling.

The script converts vector layer geometries to a specified target geometry type (Centroids, Nodes, Linestrings, Multilinestrings, or Polygons) while preserving Z/M coordinates if present. It processes each input feature, applies the selected conversion logic (e.g., computing centroids, extracting nodes, deriving boundaries for polygons, closing linestrings to form polygons), and outputs new features with the target WKB type and original attributes. The algorithm is implemented as a QGIS Processing algorithm with enum-based user selection and robust handling of geometry types, coordinate dimensions, and error cases.

The script classifies soil texture using user-provided sand and clay raster layers (loaded from QGIS map canvas) and a user-selected triangular texture classification schema file (.dat). It reads sand and clay pixel values, maps each (sand, clay) coordinate pair into a USDA or similar soil texture triangle defined by polygonal rules in the schema, assigns a numeric texture class code (e.g., 'SAND', 'CLAY', 'LOAM'), and outputs: (1) a classified GeoTIFF raster with Byte data type and -9999 NoData; (2) an optional vectorized shapefile with attribute fields 'code' and 'label_txt' derived from the schema’s legend; and (3) a CSV file ('_ternaryPlot.csv') containing per-pixel CLAY,SAND,SILT triplets for ternary plotting. The script operates entirely on local raster files — no GEE server-side computation is performed; it is a QGIS desktop plugin with GDAL/Numpy-based local raster processing. Study area, time range, satellite/sensor, and bands are not specified in the code — inputs are arbitrary local rasters selected by the user via QGIS layer list.

The script generates a synthetic Digital Surface Model (DSM) at 10m resolution by fusing a base DTM (Digital Terrain Model), building height data (rasterized from a GeoPackage of LoD1 buildings), canopy height model (CHM) from ETH, and land use masking (e.g., excluding water and bare soil). It performs raster alignment, NoData handling, height capping (≤100 m), and conditional addition of surface objects to terrain, outputting a georeferenced GeoTIFF DSM with -9999.0 as NoData value.
task_name: Generate synthetic DSM from DTM and surface features

task_description: The script computes an urban change summary table by processing urban and population raster layers across multiple time periods (2000, 2005, 2010, 2015). It splits the area of interest along meridians, aligns rasters to pixel grids using GDAL VRTs, clips them to WKT geometries, and calculates class-wise urban area (in hectares) and associated population (persons per hectare) for up to 9 urban classes. The output includes a GeoTIFF (or VRT) stack with urban and population bands per year, and an Excel summary table populated into a template with pre-defined sheet layout and cell offsets (rows 23 and 37), plus logo insertion.

The script generalizes polygon and multipolygon features in a QGIS vector layer using the Douglas-Peucker algorithm (via QgsGeometry.simplify()) with a user-specified tolerance in map units. It supports two output modes: (1) creating a new temporary or permanent memory-based layer containing simplified geometries while preserving original attributes, or (2) in-place editing of the source layer’s geometries. Vertex counts before/after simplification are computed and reported, and history is recorded for undo support via base64-encoded WKB geometry backups. The action respects feature selection, handles edit mode automatically, and includes rollback-on-error and auto-commit capabilities.

The script computes infiltration-related parameters for grid cells in a FLO-2D hydrodynamic model. It supports three methods: (1) Green-Ampt, which calculates weighted average hydraulic conductivity (XKSAT), soil water retention parameter (PSIF), change in soil moisture content (DTHETA), initial abstraction (IA), imperviousness-adjusted conductivity (XKsatc), and relative imperviousness (RTIMP) by intersecting soil and land use polygon layers with the computational grid; (2) SCS single-layer, which assigns Curve Number (CN) based on polygon centroid containment; (3) SCS multi-layer, which computes composite CN from land-soil type, cover density, and impervious fraction using empirical equations per vegetation/soil class. Outputs are dictionaries mapping grid IDs to parameter sets (e.g., {'hydc': 0.042, 'dtheta': 0.18, 'abstrinf': 0.1, 'scsn': 72}), optionally written to a diagnostic CSV file (GA_Diagnostics.csv) with columns including GridNum, SoilXKSAT, VCAdjustment, DTHETA, IA, PSIF, etc. All operations rely on QGIS vector/raster geometry intersection, spatial indexing, area-weighted averaging, logarithmic averaging (for PSIF/DTHETA when log_area_average=True), and GDAL-based raster resampling (gdalwarp) and nodata filling (gdal_fillnodata).
task_name: Calculate Green-Ampt and SCS infiltration parameters

task_description: The script performs multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) to compute and normalize spatial suitability maps for school and business development. It transforms input rasters (population density, road distance, slope, land use/land cover, water distance) using domain-specific reclassifications and inversions (e.g., '1 - slope@1' for lower-slope preference), applies distinct weighted linear combinations (school: 20% population, 30% roads, 25% slope, 15% LULC, 10% water; business: 45% roads, 35% population, 10% LULC, 10% slope), and normalizes final outputs to [0,1] using min-max scaling. Outputs include two normalized suitability rasters (school_suitability.tif, business_suitability.tif) and a difference raster (school_business_diff.tif).
